problems.problem: The batch teaches the same line twice: day 38 (23:96, Ibn Kathir: good done to the wrongdoer until enmity turns to friendship) and day 53 (41:34, al-Tabari: repel offence with pardon till the foe is like a near kinsman) give the reader near-identical key verses and near-identical readings fifteen days apart; Ibn Kathir’s enmity-to-friendship gloss on 23:96 is itself the sense of 41:34. Al-Mu’minun has a stronger line of its own that no other day in the batch covers.
problems.fix: Keep day 53 and move day 38 to Al-Mu’minun 23:115, ‘Deemed ye then that We had created you for naught, and that ye would not be returned unto Us?’ (verse.js ok, at 2787), read with al-Tabari on 23:114 to 23:115, who glosses it as God asking the wretched whether they thought He created them in play and falsehood, and that after death they would not be brought to life again to be repaid for what they did in the world (packet.js quran 38 --verse 23.115, the paragraph beginning يقول تعالى ذكره: أفحسبتم أيها الأشقياء). Plain sense from 23:112 to 23:114: the question put to the doomed about how long they tarried on earth.

problems.problem: The reading contradicts itself on the page: jinn and humankind are ‘made to humble themselves before His command’, and in the same breath deniers ‘defy only His commands’. Al-Tabari’s point turns on two different things, God’s decree (qadāʾ), to which all submit, and what He commands them to do (amr), which the denier opposes, but the sentence gives both as ‘command’, so a reader at six in the morning meets a paradox with no answer.
problems.fix: Keep al-Tabari’s distinction in his own terms, for example: al-Tabari, on 51:56 to 51:57, takes them, with Ibn Abbas, as made to worship Him and bow to His will, since even deniers yield to His decree and resist only what He bids them do.
